clue.text: Old transport group getting in the way fall down

indicators.note: the group is getting in, i.e. entering, the abbreviation for the way

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
a team is a group of players
rain is what falls down from the sky

explanation.surface: A club of old transport enthusiasts blocks the road while it pours.
explanation.definitionFit: Steam locomotives are a superseded, historic form of rail travel, so they count as old transport.

clue.text: Drains in Sweden well up

parts.note: S is the international vehicle code for Sweden

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: a spa is a mineral spring or well

explanation.surface: Water drains in Sweden come bubbling up again.
explanation.definitionFit: To sap is to drain strength or fluid away, so saps and drains are verb synonyms.

clue.text: Deserve attention, beginning now

parts.note: to have someone's ear is to have their attention

indicators.note: beginning signals the opening letter of the word now

explanation.surface: An instruction that someone has deserved our attention starting right away.
explanation.definitionFit: To earn praise is to merit or deserve it, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Writer could become Trump's oracle

indicators.note: the letters of the phrase could be rearranged to become something else

explanation.surface: A satirical suggestion that some author might turn into the US president's prophet.
explanation.definitionFit: The French novelist of In Search of Lost Time is a celebrated writer.

clue.text: Clear hesitation — one up!

parts.note: to rid a place of something is to clear it
er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: An instruction to stop dithering, with an exclamation that someone has gone ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One up' reads like a score, but means a person mounted, up on a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A horseman or jockey sits up on the horse, so is one who is up.

clue.text: Niceness enough to start riot, basically

indicators.note: a riot is wild disorder, so the letters of Niceness run riot into a new order
to start points to the opening letter of the word enough

explanation.surface: Pleasantness alone is enough to set off a riot, fundamentally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'riot' looks like the scene's climax but is the signal that reorders the letters of Niceness; 'to start' supplies the opening letter of 'enough'.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase meaning at heart or fundamentally is an adverbial equivalent of basically.

clue.text: Put away some headers to win

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A football picture: banging in a few headed goals to secure victory.
explanation.definitionFit: To stow luggage is to put it away in storage, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Huge change in monstrous battle lost

indicators.note: the change word goes in what remains of monstrous
lost says the battle's name is taken away from the word monstrous

parts.note: Mons was a First World War battle in Belgium
to emend a text is to change or correct it

explanation.surface: A huge shift after a monstrous battle has been lost.
explanation.walkthrough: Mons, the 1914 battle in Belgium, is lost from inside 'monstrous'; 'change' is not an anagram signal but the synonym that goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: Tremendous and huge are adjective synonyms for something enormous.

clue.text: Stress-reduction gadget boy's reward for getting upset

indicators.note: getting upset says the letters are knocked over into a new order

explanation.surface: A calming toy is a little lad's prize for when he gets upset.
explanation.definitionFit: A string of beads fiddled with to relieve anxiety is literally a gadget for reducing stress.

clue.text: Ammunition about to be replaced by quiet birds

indicators.note: one letter is to be replaced by another inside the ammunition word

parts.note: cartridges are rounds of ammunition
C is short for circa, Latin for about
P is piano, the musical direction for quiet

explanation.surface: Swapping noisy ammunition for something quieter when shooting birds.
explanation.definitionFit: Game birds of the pheasant family, shot for sport, so an example of birds.

clue.text: Close new organ

parts.note: the ear is the organ of hearing

explanation.surface: Wrapping up the sale of a new church organ.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organ' suggests a musical instrument but is the body part.
explanation.definitionFit: Close in the sense of nearby, not far away, is an adjective synonym.

clue.text: Possibly grave, what 3 probably had

definitions.meaning: a grave accent, as on è, is one example of a mark on French letters
3 is Marcel Proust, a Frenchman, who presumably spoke with the pronunciation of his countrymen

explanation.surface: Speculation about a serious matter concerning the writer at 3 down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grave' poses as serious but is the accent mark, so both meanings are the same phrase in two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: A grave is a diacritical mark used in French, and a Frenchman speaks with his nation's pronunciation.

clue.text: Suit to press against railway by-pass?

parts.note: hearts is one of the four suits in a pack of cards
to urge is to press or push someone

explanation.surface: A legal suit to campaign against a railway bypass route.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by-pass' looks like a road scheme, which fits the railway; the question mark flags the medical sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A coronary bypass is a cardiac operation, so a bypass is an example of this surgery.

clue.text: Chalky resolved English court case

indicators.note: a resolved case is sorted out, so the letters are sorted into a new order

explanation.surface: A dry English lawsuit that has finally been settled.
explanation.definitionFit: The geological period is named from Latin creta, chalk, and the adjective means chalk-like.

clue.text: Pile up current cloud mostly consumed

parts.note: AC is alternating current

indicators.note: mostly means the cloud word loses its final letters

parts.note: cumulus is a heaped type of cloud
to have consumed food is to have eaten it

explanation.surface: The current cloud cover has mostly been eaten away, so it heaps up again.
explanation.definitionFit: To accumulate is to gather or amass, a verb synonym for pile up.

clue.text: Erdogan possibly breaking into party

parts.note: Recep is the first name of Turkish president Recep Tayyip Erdogan, one person with that name

indicators.note: breaking says the letters of into are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: The Turkish president gate-crashing a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking into' looks like gate-crashing; 'breaking' alone rearranges INTO as TION.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal social gathering held to welcome guests is a type of party.

clue.text: Clever satellite in ensuing row

indicators.note: the satellite is placed in the reshuffled letters
a row is a disturbance, so the letters of ensuing are thrown into disorder

parts.note: Io is one of Jupiter's moons

explanation.surface: A clever moon caught up in the argument that followed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' signals rearranging 'ensuing' (it rhymes with cow), and Jupiter's moon Io goes in the result.
explanation.definitionFit: Ingenious means inventive and clever, an adjective synonym.

clue.text: Reminder for one horse to move back

indicators.note: to move back means the letters run in reverse order

parts.note: EG, for example, means for one
a dun is a horse of greyish-brown colour

explanation.surface: A cue for a single horse to reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: A gentle prod or hint to jog the memory serves as a reminder.

clue.text: Game run in closed city

indicators.note: the game and run go in the word for closed

parts.note: a door pushed to is closed
RU is rugby union
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A match goes ahead in a city under lockdown.
explanation.walkthrough: TRURO is the cathedral city of Cornwall in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Truro has cathedral city status, the only city in Cornwall.

clue.text: Fast runner uses drug mixed with honey

indicators.note: mixed with says the two words are stirred together into a new order

explanation.surface: A sprinter caught doping, taking a drug in honey.
explanation.definitionFit: A racing dog bred for speed is a fast runner on the track.

clue.text: Suit, sick in WC, had substantial snack

parts.note: clubs is one of the four suits in a pack of cards

indicators.note: sick suggests the letters are disordered and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone in a suit was ill in the toilet after a hefty snack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sick' rearranges IN WC HAD as ANDWICH. WC is the British abbreviation for a toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: A three-layer sandwich with chicken and bacon is a filling light meal.

clue.text: Compose introduction for wedding ceremony

indicators.note: the introduction for a word is its first letter

parts.note: a rite is a solemn ceremony

explanation.surface: Drafting the opening words for a marriage service.
explanation.definitionFit: To compose a poem or letter is to write it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Colossus holds up part of musician's performance

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the hidden letters read from bottom to top
the word Colossus holds the letters inside it

explanation.surface: A giant statue blocks part of a concert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holds' finds OLOS inside COLOSSUS and 'up' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A passage played by one performer alone is a part of a musician's performance.

clue.text: Polite waiters cleared places to sit

indicators.note: cleared means each word is emptied of its middle, leaving its outer letters

explanation.surface: Courteous staff cleared the tables and seating.
explanation.definitionFit: Church benches are long seats, so they are places to sit.

clue.text: Old friend, product of Australian mine?

parts.note: a pal is a friend

explanation.surface: An old mate, who might come from an Australian mining town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mine' looks like a possessive (my old friend), but is the pit; the question mark marks a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Australia produces most of the world's gemstones of this kind, dug from mines.

clue.text: Phone man taking order for caravan

parts.note: a mobile is a mobile phone

indicators.note: the man word is taking the order inside it

parts.note: he is the pronoun for a man
OM is the Order of Merit

explanation.surface: A man on the phone placing an order for a caravan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'order' looks like a purchase but is the British honour, OM.
explanation.definitionFit: A large static caravan used as a dwelling is a house that can be moved.

clue.text: Bring forth back-to-front 23

indicators.note: back-to-front here means the back letter of the word is brought to the front

parts.note: refers to the answer at 23 down, church places to sit

explanation.surface: Producing something from back-to-front church seating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back-to-front' is not a full reversal: the final S of PEWS moves to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: To spew is to pour or bring forth in a stream, as a volcano does lava.

clue.text: Claims saints rose up

indicators.note: up as in stirred up says the letters of saints rose are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: Beliefs that the saints rose up to heaven.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rose up' reads as ascension; 'rose' is part of the anagram fodder and 'up' alone is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Assertions are statements put forward as true, so they are claims.
